ontology.note: Emits an fw:NetworkSnap activity carrying fw:siteCount, fw:snappedNodeCount, fw:greatestSnapDistanceMetres, fw:snapLimitMetres and fw:metricCRS, and prov:used the site source. The distinct-node count is emitted because two sites sharing a node become indistinguishable to anything routed from there, and the greatest distance is emitted because it is the size of the error the operation introduces.

changes.description: Attaches each site to its nearest network node, measured in metres, and carries how far it moved as a snapDistanceM attribute on the point. Extracted from isochrone, which snaps inside itself and then states in a note that the distance is reported but not charged; on a node of its own that admission is visible and mappable. Third of six primitives an isochrone composition needs, and the first taken from the source end: building backwards stopped because reached edges are truncated mid-street and validateNetwork requires every edge endpoint to be a declared node, so no existing carrier can hold them. Takes a UTM zone to measure a distance, which makes eight widgets that each ask for one. See docs/experiments/82-snap-to-network.md.

evidence.note: Seven unit checks cover the nearest node being taken with the displacement carried on the point; measurement in metres picking a different node than degrees would, which is the defect this guards -- at 51.5 degrees north a node 100 m east is nearer than one 120 m north, while in raw degrees the north node looks closer; a site beyond the limit stopping the run and naming the site and the distance; two sites on one node being reported rather than refused; unlocated records being excluded and counted; the uncharged walk travelling in both the notes and the method; and refusal of a bad zone, limit or label. Not established: that the nearest node is the right attachment point. Parity against OSMnx nearest_nodes is not done.
